chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from one who narrated it, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, that he said:

Regarding a man who killed another man by mistake, then died before the diyah could be paid out to the heirs of the slain: indeed, the diyah is upon his heirs; and if he has no ʿāqilah, then it is upon the ruler from the public treasury.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money; financial compensation due for killing
key_terms.عَاقِلَةٌ: the paternal kin group legally responsible for assisting in payment
key_terms.وَرَثَتِهِ: his heirs who inherit from him

ai.seo_question: Who pays the diyah if a person who committed accidental killing dies before compensating the victim’s heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning accidental killing when the killer dies before the diyah is delivered to the heirs of the victim. It states that the financial liability remains and is borne by his heirs, and if he has no ʿāqilah, the ruler must pay it from Bayt al-Mal.
